pages.title: Register and make your first trial call
pages.summary: Start with platform registration, inspect the actual trial allowance, save the one-time key securely, and make a bounded model request without confusing a shared trial with machine ownership.
pages.audience: Individual trying shared model APIs

items.title: Register or sign in
items.text: Use the platform identity page. An existing company identity system is not required when the operator has enabled platform registration. Complete its email verification and security prompts.

items.title: Read your actual trial scope
items.text: Inspect the model aliases, expiry and remaining requests displayed in the portal. The standard profile is 24 hours, 100 requests, 20 per hour and one concurrent request; the deployment may reduce these bounds. Registration grants no machine or SSH access.

items.title: Save the key once
items.text: Choose Create trial API key. Save the secret in your password manager before closing the dialog. It is shown once and a second issuance is rejected; waiting for expiry does not create another trial. If lost, contact the operator about organization access; never paste the key into support messages.

items.title: Make a first call
items.text: Use Copy first-call example in the one-time dialog. Set API_KEY locally to your saved key and use the configured API entrance, not the browser portal URL. The example selects an allowed model alias; if the entrance is missing, ask the operator rather than guessing. Inspect the result and remaining allowance.

blocks.title: Trial is not a machine rental
blocks.text: It does not include bare-machine access or automatically open hosted ComfyUI. Continuing through an organization invitation replaces trial authority; paid machines retain their separate order and agreement checks.

For a first browser-only attempt, an active trial offers Try a prompt in the workbench. It opens the same-origin workbench using your signed-in trial session: connect, select an allowed model and send a request. It creates no API key and still enforces expiry, model scope and quota. If a request fails, search the exact public code on error-reference. HTTP 401, 403 and 429 each have multiple causes; the public code and current scope determine the next action. This source-backed route still needs deployed browser acceptance.

pages.title: Your first day in the enterprise portal
pages.summary: Choose the right organization and delivery path, review granted resources, and start API or workspace work without copying internal identifiers or assuming that registration grants infrastructure access.
pages.audience: Company owner, invited colleague or private-cloud user

items.title: Choose your organization
items.text: After sign-in, create an Individual or Company customer record, or accept an invitation. Select the intended organization before working; a customer record is not a resource grant. The operator console and enterprise portal use separate login clients and role checks.

items.title: Choose your delivery path
items.text: Private cloud: an administrator grants workspace resources without a machine-rental contract. Public trial: use the bounded shared-model allowance. Commercial machine: select an offer, accept required terms, complete checkout and wait for confirmed provisioning.

items.title: Use the granted resource
items.text: For MaaS, create a scoped API key and use Copy first-call example in its one-time dialog. For PaaS, open the approved WebIDE or ComfyUI from the workspace surface. For IaaS, use the separate machine access page only after its lease is active.

items.title: Keep your work and evidence
items.text: Save workflows and download important results. Browser-local editor drafts are not the hosted workspace volume. Inspect usage and receipts; never send a raw key or provider credential with a support request.

blocks.title: One next step, not a bypass
blocks.text: Follow the displayed readiness blocker. A manual lease request waits for operator review; no fixed approval time is promised. Payment completion, a submitted request and a ready machine are different states.

For exact failures use error-reference. For SSH and expiry consequences use exclusive-machine-basics; for managed workspace persistence use comfyui-quickstart. These guides describe implemented contracts, not proof that every external provider is live.

pages.title: Use and safely leave a rented bare machine
pages.summary: Understand the bare-machine lifecycle, claim scoped connection details, verify SSH identity, and save data before expiry without mistaking a credential handoff window for the machine lease itself.
pages.audience: User with an approved exclusive-machine lease

items.title: Wait for active access
items.text: Select a published offer or submit your requirements through the authorized request path. The platform selects eligible capacity from policy and health; you do not type a physical node address. Manual requests need operator review; provisioning may still be pending after payment.

items.title: Claim and verify
items.text: Choose Redeem SSH access once the lease is active. Copy the connection command and host fingerprint from the details. Follow the short-lived certificate issuer instructions and compare the host fingerprint before connecting; never disable SSH host verification.

items.title: Use a local tunnel when needed
items.text: For a user-owned web application listening on loopback port 8181, use the portal tunnel command built from the issued host, port and username. Keep the SSH session open and open the local forwarded address. The command does not install or start an application, and does not expose a public port.

items.title: Download before ending access
items.text: Save required files before lease expiry or End access early. Expiry closes access and starts staged tenant-account/container/volume cleanup. This is neither an instant whole-disk wipe nor a backup service. Contact the operator before expiry to discuss continued access; no self-service machine-renewal button or guaranteed extension exists.

rows: Access ends and tenant cleanup begins; export your work first.

blocks.title: Separate authorities
blocks.text: A model API allowance does not grant SSH. A machine lease does not automatically authorize every model alias. Managed inference nodes never acquire arbitrary user applications through this guide.

The connection details provide Copy SSH command, Copy host fingerprint and Copy tunnel command. Only paste these into your own trusted terminal after reviewing the destination. Clipboard permission failure does not mean the machine request failed.

pages.title: Open ComfyUI, save work and return
pages.summary: Use administrator-approved hosted ComfyUI as a WebIDE, keep workflows and results in the scoped workspace, and distinguish that delivery from a self-managed application on a rented bare machine.
pages.audience: Private-cloud or authorized workspace user

items.title: Open your approved workspace
items.text: Sign in, select the organization and open its approved ComfyUI workspace after administrator resource authorization. Private-cloud workspace access needs no rental contract. A shared interface does not mean other tenants can see your process or files.

items.title: Save and download
items.text: Save the workflow in ComfyUI and download important generated results. Hosted workflows, uploads and outputs belong to the scoped persistent workspace volume, not the browser-local workbench draft. Never treat an unsaved canvas as a backup.

items.title: Reopen and verify
items.text: Return through the portal and confirm the saved workflow and files remain. An expired or revoked lease denies HTTP, WebSocket and model access; retained volume data follows operator retention policy. Ask the administrator to restore authority rather than bypassing the gateway.

blocks.title: Hosted workspace or rented machine?
blocks.text: Hosted ComfyUI uses the authenticated workspace gateway; do not SSH or publish its private port. If you instead run your own ComfyUI under an exclusive bare-machine lease, follow exclusive-machine-basics and the portal's copyable SSH tunnel instructions. That path has machine-expiry cleanup, not hosted-volume retention.

blocks.title: Release checks still need observation
blocks.text: A tutorial and source tests do not certify a live image, real model generation or Spark performance. Validate narrow-screen scrolling, long labels, keyboard-only navigation, modal focus entry/return and downloads on the deployed UI; keep any unobserved item pending.

pages.summary: A workload crosses validation, identity, lease, policy, scheduler, runtime, and evidence boundaries. Each stage can reject safely before model execution, and terminal failures use the same canonical response shape.

steps.text: Quota and capacity are reserved; hard filters remove ineligible nodes; deterministic scoring selects a ready deployment.

blocks.text: Idempotency and ownership

Clients use a unique opaque workload ID and idempotency key per logical operation. While a workload is queued or running, a duplicate is rejected as WorkloadAlreadyActive. With workspace enforcement, durable admission state binds status and cancellation to the original authenticated subject and tenant.
Streaming and failure semantics

items: Streaming is bounded and rejects truncated completion rather than pretending success.
Alternate-node failover is allowed only before the first output is delivered.
Caller cancellation becomes CancelledByCaller.
Queue or runtime deadline expiry becomes non-retryable DeadlineExceeded.
Adapter loss becomes RuntimeUnavailable with retryability derived from the failure class.

blocks.title: Declared size is not trusted
blocks.text: Workspace admission measures UTF-8 bytes of canonical payload JSON and requires the actual size to fit both the request ceiling and lease limit.

blocks.question: Why can 能源谷“创未来”生态街区 retry only before the first streamed output?
blocks.answer: Once output reaches the caller, retrying on another node could duplicate or contradict visible results. Pre-output retry preserves one logical response boundary.

pages.title: Deploy management first, then explicitly selected compute
pages.summary: Management, model-data/storage and compute are logical roles. Install and verify the management foundation through the guarded UI first; qualify and enroll only explicitly selected compute afterward. A lab host may carry temporary compute, while a bastion remains optional operator networking rather than a 能源谷“创未来”生态街区 role.

steps.title: Prepare the selected host
steps.text: Join the chosen Kubernetes distribution, identify its real node name, prepare /data/models, pin SSH host identity, and record whether storage is dedicated or temporary.

steps.title: Render management artifacts
steps.text: Build immutable images, render management.yaml, and generate a separate mode-0600 management secret manifest. Secret values never enter the browser.

steps.title: Preview in the UI
steps.text: Select Management foundation, enter only host and local artifact references, then run Preview. It must prove SSH, storage, Kubernetes, CoreDNS, metrics and placeholder checks without mutation, then list the identities of non-secret Kubernetes resources that differ. The protected Secret manifest is never diffed.

steps.title: Confirm and apply
steps.text: After reviewing Preview, enter the exact management confirmation. Apply labels only the selected management placement and reconciles the reviewed manifests.

steps.title: Verify every service
steps.text: Require PostgreSQL, controller, console, enterprise and workbench rollouts plus ready Service endpoints. Use protected port-forwarding until the TLS edge is reviewed.

steps.title: Qualify selected compute separately
steps.text: An Ascend host may enter an explicit temporary-compute qualification profile. Future DGX Spark hosts are enrolled only after their own accelerator, runtime, trust and heartbeat evidence passes.

pages.title: Run alerts, offline orders, machine access, and guide diagnostics
pages.summary: This newcomer-first runbook connects the operator console and customer portal: respond to durable alerts, correlate bounded operational evidence, reconcile offline commercial documents, follow exclusive-machine access through expiry, and use the role-safe guide diagnostics page.
pages.audience: New on-call operators, customer administrators, finance coordinators, and exclusive-machine users

blocks.text: Start with the right surface

rows: Alert center with severity, acknowledgement, assignment, silence window, resolution, source receipt, and delivery status
Tenant inbox with read/unread state and agreement, payment, document, lease, access, expiry, or termination updates
Bounded event stream, low-cardinality metrics, immutable audit receipts, and typed alert codes
Only the status and correlation receipt needed for the customer's own request
Quote, approval, artifact generation, exact-digest review, correction, and fulfillment controls
Order timeline, print packet readiness, upload-grant request, evidence status, and correction request
Lease state, forced-revocation policy, node reachability, sanitization, and quarantine
Own machine display name, username, access-handoff status/reference, coarse reachability, expiry, termination action, and sanitization status
Authenticated aggregate health, active alert codes, state counts, recovery backlog, skill names/versions, and runbook links
Public coursebook and read-only Ask guide, without live cluster state

blocks.title: One event, two audiences
blocks.text: A durable source event can appear as an actionable operator alert and as a tenant-scoped customer notification. Reading or dismissing a message does not erase the source receipt, and a delivery retry does not create another business event.
Recipe 1: triage an alert and confirm the customer message

items: Operator: open Alerts, inspect Critical and High items first, and retain the correlation or source receipt before changing anything. Do not assume a sortable table or a separate detail dialog.
Operator: inspect the current evidence, then acknowledge ownership. Assign it to a named responder; use a bounded silence only when a maintenance window explains the signal.
Operator: resolve only after the typed condition has recovered. Resolution closes the alert lifecycle but preserves its evidence.
Customer: open Notifications in the enterprise portal, confirm the message belongs to the expected order or lease, follow its safe action, and choose Mark as read.
If email, SMS, or webhook delivery fails, continue with the in-app record and investigate the operator DeliveryDeadLetter alert.

set -eu
: "${LUNANEXA_ENDPOINT:?set the approved 能源谷“创未来”生态街区 API origin}"

  "$LUNANEXA_ENDPOINT/metrics"

blocks.text: Recipe 2: correlate events, metrics, alerts, and audit

steps.title: Operational event
steps.text: The component emits bounded JSON with a stable event code, outcome, component, time, and correlation receipt.

steps.title: Metric update
steps.text: A counter, gauge, or latency series changes using low-cardinality labels; tenant, user, lease, and request identifiers never become metric labels.

steps.title: Typed rule
steps.text: A state or metric rule detects the condition. Rules do not parse human log prose.

steps.title: Durable alert
steps.text: The notification authority deduplicates the condition and opens or updates the operator record.

steps.title: Audit correlation
steps.text: For a consequential mutation, the immutable audit receipt explains actor class, prior state, next state, decision, and result.

blocks.title: Logs explain; they do not grant authority
blocks.text: Use the correlation receipt to join the alert, operational event, adapter call, and audit record. Never paste raw logs, tokens, document bytes, prompts, model output, SSH material, or callback bodies into a ticket or the guide.
Recipe 3: complete the hybrid offline workflow

steps.title: Configure online
steps.text: The customer selects the service, SLA, project, and requested expiry; the server derives tenant and purchaser identity.

steps.title: Prepare packet
steps.text: The operator applies the immutable quote and approved policy, obtains internal approval, and releases only renderer-verified print artifacts.

steps.title: Execute offline
steps.text: The customer prints the PDF and follows the existing physical seal, treasury collection, and invoice process.

steps.title: Upload evidence
steps.text: The customer requests a short-lived upload grant. The object store and scanner report the verified digest and safety result; the browser does not choose the object reference.

steps.title: Reconcile
steps.text: A reviewer who did not submit the evidence accepts or rejects the exact digest. Rejection keeps history and requests a replacement revision.

steps.title: Fulfill
steps.text: The operator creates the opaque entitlement only after every policy-required agreement, payment, invoice, identity, and approval item is accepted.

blocks.title: A generated file is not a legal or financial outcome
blocks.text: The PDF is the print copy and the DOCX is an editable source. An upload is not an e-signature, a receipt is not bank settlement, and generated metadata is not a tax invoice. Keep the order paused until the organization's authorized legal and finance reviewers accept the required evidence.
Recipe 4: use and end an exclusive-machine lease safely

items: Customer: open My machine and verify lease state, machine display name, username, coarse reachability, handoff state, start time, and expiry before connecting. The portal intentionally does not reveal the physical node ID or a raw credential.

Customer: follow the opaque handoff reference to the approved credential broker or SSH certificate redirect. That separate trusted surface supplies the authorized host alias, port, certificate, and host-key fingerprint; compare the fingerprint before the first login.
Customer: before manual termination, save work and stop personal processes. Review the current lease generation, type the exact confirmation shown by the portal, and submit once.
Operator: watch Draining, RevokingAccess, and Sanitizing. Do not restore managed scheduling merely because the account disappeared.
Operator: return the node to managed service only after the current sanitization receipt is verified; quarantine and alert on any cleanup failure.

blocks.title: Exclusive does not mean root
blocks.text: The initial offering is an exclusive non-root account with a documented filesystem boundary and rootless containers. It does not grant sudo, management-node access, 能源谷“创未来”生态街区 daemon credentials, another tenant's data, or permission to disable the node-local expiry guard.

Skill ID, version, audience, required evidence, allowed tools/data, enablement state, and bilingual runbook route

blocks.text: Open administrator diagnostics only through the trusted signed identity proxy. If that proxy, the internal HTTPS diagnostics gateway, or its secret references are missing, keep admin diagnostics disabled; the public coursebook and read-only guide remain usable.
External prerequisites to finish before production

rows: Approved email, SMS, or webhook workers, secret references, retry policy, and dead-letter ownership
Use the durable in-app inbox and alert center; do not claim external delivery

Do not expose customer login or machine access
Trusted identity proxy, matching HMAC key, internal HTTPS read-only diagnostics gateway, secret-backed controller authority, network policy, and freshness monitor

blocks.question: What should you correlate before resolving an operator alert?
blocks.answer: Confirm the typed condition has recovered, then correlate the alert's source or correlation receipt with the bounded operational event, relevant metric, and immutable audit record. Customer read state or a successful delivery alone is not recovery evidence.

pages.title: UI-only end-to-end acceptance SOP
pages.summary: Repeat the verified local acceptance journey entirely through the installer, operator console, enterprise portal, MoonLeaf contract workspace, machine-access controls, developer workbench, and coursebook without substituting API calls for user actions.
pages.audience: Release operator, acceptance tester, customer administrator, and deployment owner

blocks.text: Before you start

blocks.title: Know what this run proves
blocks.text: This SOP proves the browser workflows and a five-node Colima/kind simulation. Demo records do not contact a production controller, issue a real SSH certificate, execute a legal contract, settle payment, or prove NVIDIA hardware. Use the same UI sequence against the production origin only after identity, secrets, external adapters, PostgreSQL, and physical-node prerequisites are ready.

rows: Deployment mode and controller connection form

blocks.text: 1. Create the minimal local cluster from the installer

items: Open Cluster installer and choose Local Colima simulation.
Enter the test-only installer token supplied by the local companion process. Never reuse an operator, inference, monitoring, callback, or production token.

Click Preview and verify. Confirm the embedded terminal says the dedicated Colima profile is ready or will start during apply and the required tools are installed. The simulator's fixed one-plus-four inventory is a test fixture, not a production topology default.
Enter the exact confirmation RECONCILE SIMULATION.
Click Reconcile simulation. Keep the page open while the embedded terminal streams progress.
For this simulator fixture only, accept when the terminal reports its management and compute placements, all placement probes running, context kind-lunanexa-sim, and command exited successfully.

blocks.title: Verified recovery behavior
blocks.text: The installer now starts a stopped dedicated Colima profile during apply and recreates an unhealthy existing lunanexa-sim topology. Preview remains read-only. If either repair fails, the terminal stays failed and the operator must not continue.
2. Walk every operator-console page

rows: Cluster running normally; 4/4 machine posture and deployment gate
Acknowledge, assign, silence, resolve, and redrive are consequential controls; use them only on the selected record
Cordon and Drain controls on each node
Model service catalog and service operations
Deploy model service, Promote, Roll back, Delete
End and clean up, End lease, Activate
Digital agreement lifecycle and enterprise requests
Retry reversal, confirm access revoked or still active, request correction, accept exact digest
Contract information, governance, approval queue, form and preview
Choose forms, save data, replace packet
Correlate actor, state transition, result, and receipt

blocks.text: 3. Walk every enterprise-portal page

rows: From agreement signing to an isolated GPU workspace
Request a time-bounded workspace and request history
Redeem SSH access credential; End access early
Refresh, upload evidence, cancel order, download verified file
Contract information and documents with MoonLeaf preview
Disable email, enable email, mark read

blocks.text: 4. Verify the MoonLeaf contract workspace

rows: NVIDIA DGX Spark compute-device remote lease agreement
Equipment damage liability and compensation notice

items: In the operator console, open Contract records. Click each form tab and wait for the associated MoonLeaf preview; no tab may show MoonLeaf demo preview failed.
Open Early termination application. Enter operator-owned settlement values: actual rent 1000, paid rent 1200, refund, refund amount 200, and an operator review decision.
Do not enter customer-owned identity, request reason, or signature fields from the operator surface. Open the enterprise Contract forms page to complete only customer-owned fields.
Confirm the preview refreshes automatically without clicking Render current draft, displays Chinese characters and spacing, and contains the new values.
Click Save data and confirm the preview and draft values remain stable after the save.

In the operator task inbox, select a tenant, search by packet or order, open a pending approval, and verify the confirmation shows action, initiator, expected revision, amount, packet-values digest, evidence and reason before Approve or Reject is enabled.

In the enterprise portal, confirm the same packet shows approval progress, payment/acceptance obligations, readable dates and CNY amounts, and the expiry countdown without any operator decision button. Click Send reminder once and confirm the success notice.

Back in the operator console, click Export audit report and inspect the downloaded tenant-scoped JSON: it may contain governance records and value-free lifecycle events, but never tokens, credentials, raw document values, signatures, seals, prompts, or outputs.

blocks.text: 5. End machine access, then inspect the workbench gate

items: In the enterprise portal, click My machines. Confirm Online, username, whole-machine SSH profile, about one day remaining, credential handoff Available, and End access early.
Click End access early, enter the exact displayed phrase TERMINATE exclusive-lease-demo, then click Terminate access.

In demo acceptance, confirm the card changes to Expiring, credential handoff Closed, cleanup Revoking access, and the termination button disappears. In production, continue watching until sanitization evidence closes the lease and the operator returns the node to managed service.

In the demo operator console, open Leases, click End and clean up, review the exact lease, node, user, and generation in the destructive-action dialog, then click Confirm action. Confirm the demo explicitly says it was previewed and no change was persisted.

Open WebIDE. Confirm Connect / refresh is disabled until a scoped inference token is present. Expand Advanced connection settings and verify controller endpoint and loopback-only opaque subject fields are visible.
Never expect the workbench lease to grant SSH, arbitrary shell, repository checkout, or managed-node filesystem access; those remain separate from exclusive-machine access.

blocks.text: 6. Renewal, contract close, and machine reclamation

items: In Contract forms, open Contract packet and select Signed and effective · packet-demo-effective.
Confirm the effective record says read-only and every customer field is disabled; historical contract data must not be edited in place.
Click Request renewal. In the confirmation dialog, review the carry-forward boundary, then click Request renewal once.

pages.audience: Beginners who finished the quickstart and now see the ComfyUI canvas for the first time

blocks.text: This page picks up where the quickstart ended: ComfyUI is open in your browser and you are staring at a dark canvas full of boxes. It does not matter whether ComfyUI was launched from the portal's workspace catalog or on an exclusive machine — the canvas is the same. Walk through this page once and you will have your first generated image and a mental map of everything on screen.
The big idea: nodes and workflows

ComfyUI thinks of image generation as an assembly line. Each box — a node — does exactly one job: one loads the model, one reads your text, one does the actual drawing, one saves the result. Wires carry the half-finished work from one node to the next. A saved arrangement of nodes and wires is called a workflow, and it is just a small JSON file you can keep, share, and reload.

items: Load Checkpoint — picks the brain: the model file (a .safetensors file, often several gigabytes) that decides what the machine can draw.
CLIP Text Encode — there are two: the upper one turns your description (the prompt) into numbers the model understands; the lower one holds what you do NOT want (the negative prompt).
Empty Latent Image — a blank canvas with a width and a height.
KSampler — the artist: it starts from static and gradually shapes it into a picture, guided by your prompt.
VAE Decode and Save Image — the framing shop: turns the finished internal picture into a normal PNG file on disk.

blocks.text: Load the default workflow

items: Open the workflow menu and choose Load Default. Recent ComfyUI versions open this workflow automatically on first launch, so it may already be on screen.
You should now see the five nodes above, already wired together. This is a complete text-to-image production line.
If a node shows a red border, do not panic — red usually means a model or an extension is missing, and the troubleshooting box below covers both.

blocks.text: Make sure a model is selected

The Load Checkpoint node has a dropdown listing every model file installed on the machine. Select any entry it offers. If the dropdown is empty, no model is installed yet — models are large downloads, and the next tutorial (Manage models, extensions, and a clean goodbye) walks through getting one.
Write your first prompt

Click the upper CLIP Text Encode box and describe the picture in plain words, most important things first — for example: a ginger cat wearing a tiny astronaut helmet, sitting on the moon, soft lighting. In the lower box (the negative prompt) list what to avoid; blurry, extra limbs, watermark is a fine starting point.
Press Queue and watch it draw

items: Click Queue Prompt, or press Ctrl+Enter.
A green highlight walks along the production line, node by node. The slow part is KSampler — a progress bar fills while it works. On a DGX-class GPU the default 20 steps take seconds, not minutes.
When the green reaches Save Image, your picture appears inside that node and in the queue panel. Click it to zoom. It is also saved as a PNG in the ComfyUI output folder on the machine.

blocks.text: The three dials worth knowing

columns: What it does, in plain words
rows: The lucky-draw number. Same seed, prompt and settings produce the same picture; change it for a different variation.
How many brush passes the artist gets. More is slower and, up to a point, more refined. 20–30 is a good starting range.
How strictly the model obeys your prompt. Around 7 is the usual start; much higher can look harsh.
Picture size in pixels. Bigger needs more GPU memory; 512×512 or 1024×1024 are safe starting points.

blocks.symptom: You press Queue and a node turns red, or the run stops with an error.
likely_causes: No model is selected in Load Checkpoint, or the model file is missing from the machine.
A node came from an extension that is not installed — common when you load someone else's workflow.
The picture size is too large for the GPU memory (an out-of-memory error).
checks: Open the Load Checkpoint dropdown and pick a model; if it is empty, install one with the next tutorial.
Read the red node's name, then install the missing extension (ComfyUI-Manager, next tutorial) or delete that node.
Halve the width and height and try again.

blocks.question: In one sentence, what is a workflow?
blocks.answer: A saved arrangement of nodes — boxes that each do one job — wired together so work flows from the model and your prompt to a finished image file. It is stored as a small JSON file you can reload or share.

pages.title: ComfyUI models, extensions, and a clean goodbye
pages.summary: The day-two skills for a ComfyUI beginner on a leased GPU machine: install a model into the right folder, add ComfyUI-Manager and custom nodes, save and share workflows as JSON, copy your images back to your own computer, and renew or end the machine lease before it wipes everything.
pages.audience: Beginners who generated their first image and want to keep working — without losing anything when the lease ends

blocks.text: You can start ComfyUI and you have made a first image. This page covers everything that keeps the experience good after day one: more models, more node types, keeping your work safe, and — most important — what happens to the machine when your time is up.

blocks.title: Two ways ComfyUI can run here
blocks.text: If you launched ComfyUI from the portal's workspace catalog, your workflows and outputs live in the workspace and the platform keeps them for you — no terminal needed. The terminal commands on this page apply when you run ComfyUI yourself on an exclusive machine over SSH.
Install a model

Models are not built into ComfyUI; each is a separate file you download once. They live in purpose-named folders under ~/ComfyUI/models — the two you will meet first are checkpoints (full models) and loras (small style add-ons). A file placed in the right folder simply appears in the matching node's dropdown.

blocks.label: Download a model into the checkpoints folder
blocks.code:
# Run on the GPU machine, inside your SSH session.
cd ~/ComfyUI/models/checkpoints
curl -L -o my-model.safetensors "<direct file link from the model page>"

# Check free disk space before big downloads:
df -h ~
# Back in the browser, click the refresh button (or restart ComfyUI),
# then pick the new file in the Load Checkpoint dropdown.

items: Only download models your organization allows you to use — licenses and safety reviews are your team's call, not 能源谷“创未来”生态街区's.
Model files are large: 2–7 GB is normal for a checkpoint.
Copy the direct file link from the model's page on the model hub, not the address of the page itself.

blocks.text: Install ComfyUI-Manager and custom nodes

The community adds new node types as small extensions called custom nodes. ComfyUI-Manager is the standard extension that installs them for you from inside the browser, so you rarely need the terminal for this.

blocks.label: Install ComfyUI-Manager once
blocks.code:
# Run on the GPU machine.
cd ~/ComfyUI/custom_nodes
git clone https://github.com/ltdrdata/ComfyUI-Manager.git

# Restart ComfyUI: press Ctrl+C in its window, then start it again
# with the same command as before. A Manager button appears in the menu.

items: Open Manager, choose Install Custom Nodes, and search for the node a workflow asks for.
When you load a workflow with missing nodes, Manager offers to install the missing custom nodes — the beginner-safe path.
Restart ComfyUI after installing so the new nodes appear.

blocks.text: Save and share workflows

items: A workflow is a small JSON file: use the menu's Save or Export to download it to your own computer.
Drag a workflow JSON — or even a PNG that ComfyUI generated — back onto the canvas to rebuild the exact setup that made it.
Keep your workflow files on your own computer, not only on the machine. The next section explains why.

blocks.text: Copy your images back to your computer
Generated images pile up in ~/ComfyUI/output on the machine. Anything you want to keep must come back to your own computer before the lease ends.

blocks.label: Download the whole output folder
blocks.code:
# Run on YOUR computer (not on the machine).
# Replace USERNAME, HOST and PORT with the portal values.
scp -P PORT -r USERNAME@HOST:~/ComfyUI/output ./comfyui-output

blocks.text: Renew or say goodbye — before the clock runs out

steps.title: Watch the countdown
steps.text: The portal's machine card shows the remaining time. Plan your last download before it reaches zero.

steps.title: Need more time?
steps.text: Contact your operator before the countdown ends: extending a machine lease is an operator action today, not a self-service button. A self-service extension request is on the roadmap — see the Planned section.

steps.title: Or end it yourself
steps.text: Choose End access early and confirm with Terminate access. This frees the machine for your colleagues immediately.

steps.title: 能源谷“创未来”生态街区 cleans up
steps.text: Login access is revoked first, then the machine is wiped and the cleanup is verified. Only after this deep clean does the machine return to the shared pool.

blocks.title: Expiry erases everything
blocks.text: When the lease ends — by the clock or by your own hand — your login stops working and the entire machine is sanitized: every model, workflow, and image on it is permanently deleted. 能源谷“创未来”生态街区 does this on purpose, so the next user gets a provably clean machine. Download everything you want to keep first.

blocks.question: What is the one thing to do before a lease expires?
blocks.answer: Copy everything you want to keep — the images in ~/ComfyUI/output and your saved workflow JSON files — back to your own computer. Expiry revokes access and wipes the machine; nothing left on it can be recovered afterwards.

pages.title: Planned: SSH, JupyterLab, and remote development on managed nodes
pages.summary: A look at the interactive future being considered: opening a terminal or a JupyterLab notebook against managed GPU capacity, with the same fencing, expiry, and cleanup discipline as today's exclusive leases. Nothing on this page works yet — here is the shape it would take and what to use meanwhile.
pages.audience: Users who wish they could open a terminal or notebook on a managed machine, and operators evaluating that request

blocks.text: Today a managed GPU node is a sealed box: it runs the platform agent, one approved model runtime, and signed model files — and nobody logs in. Many people reasonably ask for a terminal or a JupyterLab notebook on that hardware anyway. This page describes how such interactive access would have to look if 能源谷“创未来”生态街区 ever offers it, and why it has to earn its way in.

blocks.title: Not available today
blocks.text: Managed nodes still accept no interactive logins, and there is no JupyterLab or remote-development profile on them. What does exist today: hosted web workspaces — browser IDE and ComfyUI — running as isolated workspace backends you reach through the portal, plus the exclusive machine lease for a whole fenced machine.
What you would be able to do

steps.title: Ask for a session
steps.text: Request an interactive profile — a shell or a JupyterLab notebook — which is checked against the same account, grant, and lease chain as a model call.

steps.title: Get a fenced seat
steps.text: 能源谷“创未来”生态街区 starts a reviewed, containerized session image with no path to the node agent, other tenants, or the model store.

steps.title: Work with a clock
steps.text: The session carries the same discipline as everything else: a visible countdown, expiry warnings, and a hard stop.

steps.title: Leave no trace
steps.text: When it ends, the session container and its writable layer are destroyed with the same receipt evidence as a lease cleanup — uncertainty still means quarantine.

blocks.text: The boundaries that would not move

items: A session is a workload, not a host login: the node agent, model artifacts, and other tenants stay unreachable.
Session images are digest-pinned and signed; nothing is installed ad hoc on the node.
Every session still produces audit and cleanup receipts, exactly like a lease.

pages.summary: Three convenience features from public clouds — keeping your app running across restarts, reaching it from the internet, and importing Kubernetes YAML — and the governed shape each one would need before 能源谷“创未来”生态街区 could offer it. None of these exist today; here is the honest why, and what to use instead.
pages.audience: Users coming from public clouds who miss these three conveniences, and operators designing their governed replacements

blocks.text: Three requests arrive together so often that they share a page: keep my application running across restarts, let me reach it from the internet, and let me import the Kubernetes YAML I already have. All three are about making something reachable and durable — and all three need a governed shape before they can exist here.

blocks.title: Not available today
blocks.text: There is no autostart setting, no public port exposure, and no YAML import. Runtime configuration today is immutable and reviewed, and all traffic enters through the 能源谷“创未来”生态街区 gateway. Note that hosted workspace apps — browser IDE, ComfyUI — are already reachable through that authenticated gateway; what is planned is user-declared exposure for your own workloads.
From public-cloud habit to the planned 能源谷“创未来”生态街区 shape

columns: Planned 能源谷“创未来”生态街区 shape
rows: A declared restart policy in the workload profile, applied and evidenced by the controller — not a shell script on the host

pages.title: Planned: autoscaling and batch job queues
pages.summary: Two fleet-scale features — capacity that grows and shrinks by itself, and queues of batch jobs — and why 能源谷“创未来”生态街区's current product contract deliberately excludes both. This page explains what would have to be proven first, and the predictable-overload behavior you get today.
pages.audience: Users planning large or bursty workloads, and operators who need to explain the fixed-fleet behavior

blocks.text: Autoscaling means the fleet adds or removes machines as demand changes, without a human involved. Batch queues mean you hand over a pile of jobs — render these ten thousand images, process this dataset — and the system works through them while you sleep. Both are real cloud features, and both are deliberately absent from 能源谷“创未来”生态街区's current contract.

blocks.title: Not available today — by explicit decision
blocks.text: The current product contract lists batch jobs, task groups, spot queues, and an autonomous autoscaler as out of scope. They are Phase 6 candidates in the expansion plan: each would arrive as its own program with its own product contract, security boundary, service objective, and acceptance campaign — not as a quiet feature flag.
What you would be able to do

steps.title: Describe the work with bounds
steps.text: Submit a job queue or a scaling rule with explicit limits: maximum nodes, deadline, and priority — never an open-ended claim on the fleet.

steps.title: The fleet decides within evidence
steps.text: Scaling and scheduling decisions come from measured capacity and health, with exclusive-lease fencing always respected.

steps.title: Predictable endings
steps.text: Every job ends in a typed terminal state with a receipt — completed, failed with a stated reason, or cancelled. Never limbo.

blocks.text: What has to be proven first

items: The four-node internal pilot and the shared production foundations (Phases 1–2 of the expansion plan) come first.
An autoscaler must never override health, security, placement, or exclusive-lease fencing — policy outranks demand.
Retry caps, circuit breakers, and typed terminal failure reasons are prerequisites: a fleet must fail predictably rather than burn leases on bad work.

blocks.text: What you get today instead

Today's fleet is fixed and honest about it. Each lease carries bounded concurrency and rate limits; when capacity is full, requests wait in a bounded queue or fail with a typed, retryable answer you can act on. For interactive and inference work this predictability is a feature: your lease means what it says.
